selection_rule: highest mean validation BB/100 over the opponents; ties -> earlier round

importance_definitions.global_importance: mean |term score| (log-odds) averaged over the five actions, on 20000 random validation states; main effects and pairwise interactions are ranked together
importance_definitions.global_importance_by_action: the same average for one action's logit
importance_definitions.global_importance_training_weighted: InterpretML's term_importances(): mean |score| over the training bins, weighted by the (class-weighted) training data - what ebm.explain_global() shows

notes: Imitation metrics measure agreement with the equity teacher, not poker skill. The hyper-parameters were chosen on the validation split, so 'imitation' is slightly optimistic; 'imitation_on_policy' and 'policy_validation' use fresh validation seeds, but the selected round was picked on those very BB/100 numbers (winner's curse), and the mean BB/100 of different rounds differs by far less than the width of its confidence intervals - 'dagger[*].paired_vs_bc' compares every round with round 0 on identical deals. EBM scores are contributions to each action's log-odds; correlated features (equity, equity_minus_pot_odds, pot_odds, preflop_percentile) share credit, so read their shape functions together.
evaluation_protocol_note: policy_validation and every dagger[*].policy_validation entry were computed with the legacy single-table duplicate protocol (the two hands of a deal shared agents and opponent trackers), which gives the second-moving agent a small advantage (roughly +10 to +13 BB/100 between identical adaptive agents). They are informational: the DAgger round was selected among near-tied candidates. Tournament results in artifacts/tournaments use the corrected two-table protocol. See docs/METHODOLOGY.md, section 5.
